title: Source Library for Palestine
subtitle: A practical reading map for Islamic sources, history, law, and current reporting
summary: A reliable study of Palestine uses the right source for each question. Quran and hadith establish Islamic belief; historians explain change over time; original documents show what institutions decided; courts and legal texts address law; and dated humanitarian reports describe current conditions. This guide points readers to each type and explains its limits.

sections.title: How to Build a Reliable Reading List
sections.body: No single book, website, government, or organization answers every question about Palestine. Start by asking whether the question is about Islamic belief, identity and history, a legal rule, a humanitarian condition, or a breaking event. Then choose a source built to answer that question.

sections.title: Verification Is an Islamic Responsibility
sections.body: Quran 49:6 tells believers to investigate reports so that people are not harmed through ignorance. The full Arabic and English verse appears below. For any important claim, record the original source, author, date, place, evidence, and later correction. If proof is missing, label the claim unverified rather than filling the gap with confidence.

sections.title: Islamic Scripture and Scholarship
sections.body:
Use the Quran for what Allah reveals and authentic hadith for the Prophet's teachings. [The opening verse of Surah al-Isra, displayed in the Jerusalem article](/articles/jerusalem-and-al-aqsa), names al-Masjid al-Aqsa and blesses its surroundings. [Sahih al-Bukhari 1189](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:1189) gives Al-Aqsa a special place among three mosques, while [Sahih Muslim 525b](https://sunnah.com/muslim:525b) records Jerusalem as the early prayer direction.

Read scripture with reliable tafsir and hadith commentary. Keep Quranic text, Prophetic report, later interpretation, classical jurisprudence, and modern political argument distinct. They may relate to one another, but they are not the same kind of evidence.

sections.title: History and Primary Documents
sections.body:
For Palestinian identity and local life, begin with [Rashid Khalidi](https://cup.columbia.edu/book/palestinian-identity/9780231150743) and [Beshara Doumani](https://www.ucpress.edu/book/9780520203709/rediscovering-palestine). For a broad conflict history written for general readers, use [James Gelvin's survey](https://www.cambridge.org/highereducation/books/israelpalestine-conflict/5D389E3231527643CCE3F861003EC172). Compare their questions and evidence rather than treating any author as neutral by definition.

For original UN material, use the [UNISPAL document collection](https://www.un.org/unispal/data-collection/) and its [historical orientation](https://www.un.org/unispal/history/). A resolution or report proves what a UN body recorded or decided; its author, mandate, date, and evidentiary method still matter.

sections.title: Law and Judicial Sources
sections.body:
For the rules of armed conflict, begin with the [ICRC's rules-of-war guide](https://www.icrc.org/en/document/FAQ-rules-of-war-ihl) and then consult the relevant treaty or customary-law rule. For judicial findings, read the judgment or advisory opinion itself. The [International Court of Justice case page on the occupied Palestinian territory, including East Jerusalem](https://www.icj-cij.org/case/186) collects the 2024 advisory opinion, summary, and separate opinions.

A court document answers a legal question within that body's jurisdiction and procedure. It does not replace historical research, and a headline about a case does not replace the court's own wording.

sections.title: Humanitarian Data and Current Reporting
sections.body:
For humanitarian conditions, consult dated reports from [UN OCHA's occupied Palestinian territory office](https://www.ochaopt.org/) and [UNRWA's information on Palestine refugees](https://www.unrwa.org/palestine-refugees). Check what population, period, and method each figure covers. UNRWA's operational refugee category is not a definition of every Palestinian.

For breaking news, seek the earliest attributable evidence and independent confirmation. Separate what a witness, military, government, hospital, or aid agency claims from what a reporter has verified. Figures may be revised; record the publication date.

sections.title: A Simple Method for Readers
sections.body:
For an important claim, ask: Who made it? What proof is given? When was it recorded? Can the original be opened? What is the source's mandate or point of view? Has an independent source checked the same evidence?

Avoid anonymous screenshots, undated videos, cropped quotations, and claims that treat whole peoples as one mind. Sources do not become useless because they have a perspective; their perspective and limits must be made visible.

sections.title: Key Takeaways: Reading Palestine Responsibly
sections.body: Read Islamic sources for religious meaning, historians for context, original records for institutional actions, legal texts for law, and current reports for dated conditions. Check before repeating, distinguish evidence from interpretation, and correct errors openly. Truthful study strengthens justice and reflects Islamic character.

quranVerses.arabic: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوٓا۟ إِن جَآءَكُمْ فَاسِقٌۢ بِنَبَإٍۢ فَتَبَيَّنُوٓا۟ أَن تُصِيبُوا۟ قَوْمًۢا بِجَهَٰلَةٍۢ فَتُصْبِحُوا۟ عَلَىٰ مَا فَعَلْتُمْ نَٰدِمِينَ
quranVerses.translation: O you who have believed, if there comes to you a disobedient one with information, investigate, lest you harm a people out of ignorance and become, over what you have done, regretful.

furtherReading.title: United Nations: Question of Palestine
furtherReading.author: United Nations
furtherReading.note: Official documents, resolutions, reports, and background material. Read each document with attention to its date, author, and institutional mandate.

furtherReading.title: History of the Question of Palestine
furtherReading.author: United Nations
furtherReading.note: A continuously maintained institutional overview of the Mandate, partition, 1948, 1967, and later UN involvement; use it as a documented UN chronology, not as the only historical interpretation.

furtherReading.title: Palestinian Identity: The Construction of Modern National Consciousness
furtherReading.author: Rashid Khalidi
furtherReading.note: A major scholarly study of Palestinian identity and its historical development.

furtherReading.title: Rediscovering Palestine: Merchants and Peasants in Jabal Nablus, 1700–1900
furtherReading.author: Beshara B. Doumani
furtherReading.note: A social and economic history that grounds discussion of Palestine in families, towns, trade, and local institutions.

furtherReading.title: The Israel-Palestine Conflict: A History
furtherReading.author: James L. Gelvin
furtherReading.note: An accessible historical survey that places Palestinian and Israeli national movements in their wider context.

furtherReading.title: Frequently Asked Questions: Rules of War
furtherReading.author: International Committee of the Red Cross
furtherReading.note: A plain-language introduction to distinction, proportionality, precautions, and civilian protection under international humanitarian law.

furtherReading.title: Legal Consequences Arising from the Policies and Practices of Israel in the Occupied Palestinian Territory, Including East Jerusalem
furtherReading.author: International Court of Justice
furtherReading.note: The official case page for the advisory opinion, summary, and judges' separate opinions; use the court's own wording rather than a headline summary.

furtherReading.title: United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs: Occupied Palestinian Territory
furtherReading.author: United Nations OCHA
furtherReading.note: Situation reports, maps, and humanitarian data. Check publication dates and methodology for every statistic.

furtherReading.title: UNRWA: Palestine Refugees
furtherReading.author: United Nations Relief and Works Agency
furtherReading.note: Official information about the agency's mandate and services to Palestine refugees; distinguish institutional reporting from independent analysis.
